candidate.topic: Blood-pressure measurement gap before GP visit
candidate.why_now: Your October 5 GP appointment is a decision point about medication. Collecting blood-pressure readings now could make that discussion more informed.
candidate.what_changed: You recorded the October 5 appointment on September 22. The available watch data tracks steps and resting heart rate, not blood pressure, so it cannot show whether your blood pressure has come down since you began walking daily.
candidate.unknowns: Your current blood-pressure pattern is unknown. Without comparable readings from before you began walking, new readings also could not establish whether walking lowered it or caused any change.
candidate.next_step: If you have a home blood-pressure monitor, record readings with the same monitor after sitting quietly for five minutes, morning and evening for seven days, and bring the dated readings to the appointment. They could inform the medication discussion, though they would not answer whether blood pressure fell since walking began.
